proposals.title: Write ADR-002, ADR-004, and ADR-009 before any packages/core implementation
proposals.why_now: FASE-1 acceptance criteria explicitly require ADR-009 to be written and the CanonicalEncoder implemented before any StateHash exists. ADR-002 requires the hash function specified bit-by-bit in its own ADR before any rand() call is written. ADR-004 must resolve how omitting a rounding mode becomes a compile-time or blocking-lint error before the divInt helper can be typed correctly. All three packages/core components (RNG, encoder, division) depend on these ADRs; without them any implementation embeds silent decisions that cannot be reversed without an encodingVersion bump that invalidates frozen reference hashes. These are documentation-only changes with zero risk of regression.

proposals.title: Register transcendental-function and tools/* dependency-edge blockers in SPEC_BLOCKERS.md
proposals.why_now: Two concrete specification issues block FASE-1 implementation and are currently unregistered. First, §5.1 constructs prices in log-space (requires Math.log, Math.exp) while §13 prohibits Math.log, Math.exp, Math.sin, Math.cos in pure packages — this is a specification contradiction that blocks packages/world entirely. Second, the boundary graph in §14.5 defines no directed edges for tools/* yet tools/replay must import packages such as packages/core and packages/application to replay a save — the existing boundary checker graph.mjs already encodes tools:[] (no imports permitted) which would make the FASE-1 required tools/replay impossible. Both must be registered per §19 before any implementation that would silently resolve them.

proposals.title: Implement packages/domain — double-entry multi-commodity ledger and spot market order execution
proposals.why_now: The ledger is the second structural prerequisite of FASE-1. INV-04 (every transaction balances per commodity), INV-05 (BRL sum across all accounts is zero), INV-06 (asset quantity sum is zero), and INV-07 (rounding residue accounted) are all ledger invariants that must be green for FASE-1 acceptance. Spot market orders are the only order type required by FASE-1 and they require the ledger. packages/domain depends only on packages/core, so it can be implemented as soon as core is complete and requires no resolution of the transcendental-function blocker (IDEA-002) that affects packages/world.

proposals.title: Implement Electron application skeleton — simulation worker, typed IPC, and Electron security (INV-29)
proposals.why_now: FASE-1 requires that simulation already runs in a dedicated worker outside the rendering thread with a typed message contract. INV-29 requires contextIsolation:true, nodeIntegration:false, sandbox:true in all execution modes including development — this is a security invariant with a CI gate. The Electron process topology (main, preload, renderer, simulation-worker) and the contracts package shape every downstream feature because the renderer may never import domain or application packages directly. Establishing the correct process boundaries, the contextBridge allowlist, the typed IPC channel contract in packages/contracts, and the simulation-worker host now prevents architectural drift in later phases. Without this, domain and world implementations have no wiring and cannot produce an end-to-end tick.

FASE-1 explicitly forbids any StateHash from existing before ADR-009 is written and the encoder implemented, and forbids any rand() implementation before ADR-002 specifies the hash function bit-by-bit. Nothing in the domain, world, application, or replay layers can be started until core exports its nominal types, RNG, and encoder.

warnings: SPECIFICATION CONFLICT — §5.1 requires log-space price construction (logPrice formula with trendLayer, marketFactor, regimeAmplitude) which implicitly requires transcendental functions; §13 explicitly prohibits Math.log, Math.exp, Math.sin, Math.cos, Math.pow, Math.sqrt in all pure packages including packages/world. The resolution (fixed-point implementation or lookup table, per §14.4 ADR-003 guidance) must come from an ADR, not from silent choice. packages/world is blocked until this is registered and resolved.

SPECIFICATION GAP — §14.5 defines directed dependency edges for packages/* and apps/* but does not define any edges for tools/*. The current boundary checker encodes tools:[] (no outbound imports permitted). tools/replay must import at minimum packages/core and packages/application to be capable of replaying a save, and tools/bench must import packages/core to calibrate performance. Both FASE-1 required tools are currently blocked by the boundary checker with no specified resolution.
